clue.text: Nick's hesitancy to leave Delaware

definitions.note: a nick is a small cut; the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: to leave says the state's letters must go out of the longer word

parts.note: hesitancy is a failure to make up one's mind
DE is the postal abbreviation of the US state of Delaware

explanation.surface: A man called Nick is so dithering that he cannot bring himself to depart from Delaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick's' reads as a man's name with a possessive, but it is the noun nick plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a nick is a small cut, and a surgeon's cut into flesh is called an incision.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, is secure

definitions.note: the Isle of Man is one example of a piece of land surrounded by sea

parts.note: to land a contract or a fish is to secure it

explanation.surface: A statement that some man is safe and secure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Isle of Man is one instance of a landmass ringed by water.

clue.text: His rector ordered one will perform in church

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A vicar instructs someone that they will sing in his church.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a member of a church choir sings in services.

clue.text: I dust ma's mixing bowl

indicators.note: mixing says the letters before it are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: I dust while mum stirs her mixing bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of ma's is 'is', a link; 'mixing bowl' looks like one kitchen item but splits into indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large sports arena with tiered sides is often called a bowl.

clue.text: Strangely overdrawn — delay with regular withdrawals

parts.note: OD is the bank-statement abbreviation for overdrawn

indicators.note: regular withdrawals means every other letter of delay is taken away, keeping the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A bank account is mysteriously overdrawn, the money delayed by repeated withdrawals.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done strangely is done in a peculiar or unusual way.

clue.text: Editor defaced book? It's ok to scoff

indicators.note: defaced means the front, or face, of the word is removed

parts.note: the Bible is the book above all others

explanation.surface: An editor has vandalised a book and asks whether eating it is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' is British slang for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: food that is fit to be eaten is safe to wolf down.

clue.text: Freak to propose entering river

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales
to vote that something be done is to propose it

explanation.surface: An odd character suggests going into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fitness freak is an enthusiast, a keen follower of something.

clue.text: Put a stop to almost everything trivial

parts.note: to ban something is to put a stop to it

indicators.note: almost says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Advice to halt nearly every unimportant matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something trivial is commonplace, trite and lacking originality.

clue.text: I'm taken aback after European initially gave cost to settle abroad

indicators.note: after puts the turned letters behind the European abbreviation
taken aback means the two letters are turned round, read backwards
initially means only the first letter of gave is used

parts.note: a rate is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: Someone surprised that a European gave them the price of moving overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reads as surprise, but it turns I'M round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to leave one's own country to live in another is to settle abroad.

clue.text: Lovely, talented, enthralling girl

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the first word holds the girl inside it

parts.note: able means skilled or talented
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A description of a lovely, gifted and captivating young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something adorable is delightful and charming.

clue.text: Artist Dali craved onion rolls

indicators.note: rolls means the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: The painter Dali longed for onion bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' and 'Dali' both point to a painter; Dali is fodder, the definition is 'Artist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa is an artist.

clue.text: Bins occasionally taken in by brave person going round yard far from quietly

indicators.note: taken in by means the picked letters go inside the turned word
going round says the word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: a brave person is a lion, as in lion-hearted

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters of Bins are used, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A noisy scene of bins being collected by a hero circling a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave person' and 'going round' read as a hero circling, but the lion is simply turned backwards; 'Bins' looks like rubbish yet only lends two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite: doing something far from quietly means doing it with lots of noise.

clue.text: Snake upset rook

parts.note: to rattle someone is to upset them
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A snake has disturbed a crow-like bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name: a rattlesnake is often called by this shortened word.

clue.text: Rush after a cat — it could cause immense damage

indicators.note: after puts the rushing word behind the cat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to bomb along is to rush at speed

explanation.surface: Someone dashing after a cat, which could cause great destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a nuclear fission weapon devastates whole cities.

clue.text: Musical piece coming from speaker on bottom of hi-fi? Ordinary

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A piece of music playing through a speaker on a hi-fi system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker' and 'hi-fi' suggest audio equipment, but the speaker is a person who makes speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large-scale sacred work for voices and orchestra, such as Handel's Messiah.

clue.text: Some sober up then throw up

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice to a drunk: sober up, and then be sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a volcano that erupts throws up lava and ash.

clue.text: Liberal rings up an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician phones an oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' reads as a political party, but here it means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone liberal with praise is lavish and generous, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Plant laid off unfortunately about 500

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the numeral
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A factory has unhappily sacked around five hundred staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a yellow spring-flowering bulb is a kind of plant.

clue.text: American politician not ultimately giving consent

indicators.note: not ultimately says the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party

explanation.surface: A US politician who in the end refuses to give approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to consent to something is to say yes to it.

clue.text: Discharge from outlet an American partly picked up

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
partly says only some of the letters of these words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Fluid leaking from a drain, picked up by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes ETANAME from outlET AN AMErican and 'picked up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to emanate is to flow out or issue from a source.

clue.text: A contemptuous person imbibing what alcohol is sold here

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person
eh is an exclamation meaning what, as in asking for a repeat

explanation.surface: A sneering drinker swallowing whatever booze is on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contemptuous person' is a loose way of saying contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an old word for a pub, a place serving beer and spirits.

clue.text: One caught in grasp of tender policeman

indicators.note: in grasp of means held inside the other word

parts.note: to tender is to offer
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone captured in the clutches of a gentle constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like an adjective meaning gentle, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a police officer is a constable or policeman.

clue.text: Nasty piece of work that is below average

indicators.note: below in a down clue puts the second piece underneath the first

parts.note: the mean is the average
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An unpleasant person who is not up to the ordinary standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a mean, unkind person is a horrible individual.

clue.text: Artist to leave after much chaos

indicators.note: after puts the artist and leaving behind the word for much

parts.note: far means much, as in far better
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A painter departs after a great deal of disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a jumble or confused mixture is a muddle, a state of disorder.

clue.text: Wrong to follow king round — it's essential to bow

indicators.note: to follow puts the wrong after the other pieces

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king
O is round in shape
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A courtier is told it is wrong to trail around after the king, and must bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests bending before a king but is the bow of a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: string players rub resin on a violin bow so it grips the strings.

clue.text: Excite stylish sweetheart

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish
an old flame is a former sweetheart

explanation.surface: A command to thrill a fashionable lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to arouse strong feelings is to stir up or excite them.

clue.text: At home, female starts to enjoy regular work out

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A woman at home starting to enjoy a regular exercise routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' reads as exercise but means deduce.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to infer is to deduce or reason out from evidence.

clue.text: Finds waistcoat is tight? Losing weight at first creates frustration

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters lurch into a new order
Losing says a letter is shed from the jumbled pool
at first means only the initial letter of weight

explanation.surface: A man finds his waistcoat too snug, and losing weight first brings annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' reads as snug but signals the anagram; the letters minus W rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: discontent at not getting what one wants is frustration.

clue.text: Golfer left to tee off

parts.note: to tee off, American slang, is to annoy or anger

explanation.surface: A golfer quits so he can take his opening drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernhard Langer is a German golfer, twice Masters champion; 'tee off' points to golf but means annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Bernhard Langer is a famous German professional golfer.

clue.text: Reason for mischief-maker to postpone session

parts.note: a pro is an argument in favour, as in pros and cons
a rogue is a rascal or mischief-maker

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a troublemaker should delay a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliamentary term: to discontinue a session of parliament without dissolving it.
